transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, my wife was really worried and persuaded me to come in, but the main thing is that I know my paintings have an important message for the people running this country, and no one seems to understand that. It’s incredibly frustrating because these pieces are meant for national leaders, but everyone around me just dismisses it.
How long have you been feeling that your paintings have a special message meant for national leaders, and has this belief come on suddenly or been present for a long time?

It hasn't been a long-time thing; it's really been building up over the last two months. It all started after my close friend passed away suddenly and my younger brother was diagnosed with advanced cancer. Before those losses, I never had these ideas about my art holding messages for the people in power.
Have you had any other unusual experiences during these two months, like hearing voices, feeling that people are watching or controlling you, or believing things that others say are not true?

Yes, late at night in my workshop, I'll hear my brother's voice as clear as day telling me to "keep going, they're watching," even though I know he's hours away undergoing chemo. I am also completely convinced that my paintings have hidden messages in the colors and shapes meant for the President, and even though my wife says it's far-fetched, it feels absolutely true to me.
During these past two months, have you also had periods of feeling unusually high or irritable, needing much less sleep, having racing thoughts, or feeling much more energetic than usual?

Yes, absolutely—my mind has been running like a TV with all the channels on at once, and I have this restless energy where I'm on my feet all day and staying up late in my workshop neglecting sleep. I also swing between feeling incredibly pumped up and giddy about my projects to snapping at my wife when she asks about bills or tries to slow me down.
Have these high-energy, little-sleep, and racing-thought periods lasted at least 1 week continuously, or have they been shorter and more brief?

Oh, it has lasted much longer than just a single week. This has been going on non-stop every single day for about two months now, ever since my friend passed away and my brother got sick. It's an everyday, continuous rush of energy that just hasn't let up at all.

Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or increased activity, even without the unusual beliefs or voices?

No, I've never had those thoughts or heard my brother's voice outside of this high-energy state. They only started when I got so wound up and driven with these projects over the last two months. On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those ideas and voices seem to fade away.

Have the unusual beliefs or hearing your brother's voice ever happened when you were not feeling unusually energized, restless, or needing much less sleep? In other words, do they ever continue on their own when your mood and energy are back to normal?

No, they never happen when my energy is normal. I only hear my brother's voice and believe those things about my art when I'm feeling highly energized and wound up. On the rare days when my energy dips back down, those thoughts and voices completely fade into the background.
Have these high-energy, little-sleep, and racing-thought periods lasted at least 1 week continuously, or have they been shorter and more brief?

Yes, it has been much longer than just a week. This has been a continuous, non-stop experience for about two months now, ever since my friend passed away and my brother got his diagnosis. It is definitely not just brief bursts of energy; it has been going on constantly.

The candidate list is therefore narrowed to the bipolar category code.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear manic syndrome lasting about 2 months with decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, increased energy/activity, pressured/restless behavior, and irritability, accompanied by mood-congruent psychotic symptoms (grandiose/paranoid delusions and auditory hallucinations) that occur only during the elevated mood state. This supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms. Adjustment disorder and primary manic episode were considered, but the sustained full manic syndrome with psychosis is most consistent with F31.2.
